triage.reason: Specifies the slug regex, exact 400/409 statuses and bodies, and the unchanged default and success behavior, all in one small change to POST /links in src/app.js.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /links with {url, slug} where slug matches ^[a-z0-9-]{3,32}$ and is free returns 201 with {slug: <given slug>, url, shortUrl: "/<slug>"}
The created link is retrievable: GET /<slug> redirects (302) to the url
A slug that does not match the regex returns 400 with {"error": "invalid slug"}; cases: 2 chars, 33 chars, uppercase, underscore or space, and the boundaries of 3 and 32 chars are accepted
A non-string slug (number, null, object) returns 400 {"error": "invalid slug"}
A slug that is already taken returns 409 with {"error": "slug taken"}, and the existing link's url, clicks and createdAt are unchanged
Without a slug field, the slug comes from the injected randomSlug as before and the response is 201 {slug, url, shortUrl}
An invalid url still returns 400 {"error": "invalid url"}; the issue does not say which error wins when both url and slug are invalid, so the url check stays first as today

work.summary: Implemented custom slugs in POST /links in src/app.js. A string slug matching ^[a-z0-9-]{3,32}$ is used, an invalid or non-string slug returns 400 {error:'invalid slug'}, a taken slug returns 409 {error:'slug taken'}, and no slug falls back to randomSlug. The url check still runs first. Added test/custom-slug.test.js covering these cases, but I could not run npm test because shell execution was denied, so the tests are unverified.
